observer_names: Harold Dahl, Dahl's 16-year-old son, and a Mr. Knight, aboard a boat owned by Fred Crisman
object_shape: Four or five circular objects approximately 100 feet in diameter, with a hole in the center through which sky was visible, and portholes visible on the inside of the circle. One object appeared to be in trouble.
object_behavior: Objects hovered at approximately 1500 feet altitude at negligible speed. A second object made contact with the distressed object for approximately two minutes then rose to original position. The distressed object ejected debris from one of its portholes. Objects then disappeared from view. Debris damaged the boat wheelhouse, spotlight, and klaxon, killed a dog and a sea gull.

object_behavior: Object had crashed into ground at approximately 45 degree angle with left wing embedded in earth. Had slid 300-400 feet on impact. Was dented but generally intact. location_raw: 46 of 48 United States, including near Oak Ridge, Tennessee
observer_names: Colonel Gasser (personally observed single vapor trail from horizon to horizon), Air Force intelligence officials, Central Intelligence Agency representatives in Southern Europe and Southern Asia, general public across 46 states
object_behavior: Traveled in straight line at tremendously high altitudes and unbelievably tremendous speed. Could maintain altitude above ground contour possibly via radio altimeter. location_raw: Forest clearing near Hasselbach, Soviet zone of Germany, near Gleimershausen, Meiningen
observer_names: Oskar Linke, 48-year-old former mayor of Gleimershausen, and his 11-year-old stepdaughter Gabriele. Corroborating witnesses included a shepherd named Georg Derbst (about 1.5 miles away) and a sawmill watchman, both of whom saw what they thought was a low-flying comet.
object_behavior: Object was initially resting on the ground on the conning tower/cylinder struts. Two figures rushed back to it, climbed up the side of the conning tower, and disappeared inside. The cylinder then retracted into the object. The object rose slowly at first then ascended rapidly with a whistling sound, swerved toward a nearby village, and disappeared at terrific speed over hills and forests toward Stockheim. A circular depression was found in the ground afterward matching the shape of the conning tower.
